title: Suspect Starts Shooting at ATF Federal Agents
description:
MIDWEST SAFETY: Uncover. Inform. Empower.

CONTACT US:
Complaints? Video submissions? Tips? Sponsorships? Collabs? Business inquires? 
Email our board at mn.safety.alerts@gmail.com. 

BE NICE:
The individuals presented in these videos may be suffering from the effects of alcohol, drug abuse, a mental health disorder or simply having a bad day. The videos should NOT be presumed to be representative of their general behavior. Everyone deserves to be treated with respect. 

RIGHT TO BE FORGOTTEN:
Midwest Safety practices the "Right to be Forgotten." If you were the suspect in a lower-level offense, you may email our board to reqeust removal. Email: mn.safety.alerts@gmail.com

Police officers and agents from the Federal Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, and Firearms are in the middle of a high-speed chase in Plant City, Florida. The suspect fleeing is Francisco Cabrera. Just days before, he robbed two stores and a gas station at gunpoint. Right before he was located, he returned to the gas station he previously robbed and carjacked an individual at gunpoint. When officers located him in Plant City and activated their lights and sirens, he immediately fled. We now follow an officer tasked with cutting the suspect off. This officer is turning on to New Tampa Highway heading westbound. The suspect is currently down the road, heading towards the officer, while being chased by multiple officers and ATF special agents. These two officers now pull over because they know the suspect is just seconds away. They exit their vehicles attempting to deploy stopsticks while the suspect heads right towards them. The suspect just fired at both officers, prompting officers to return fire. While they didn't get hit, both the officers and the ATF agents know it's time to put an end to the suspect's fleeing, even if it means using lethal force. As the officer pulls up, an ATF special agent has already fired two shots at the suspect, both of which hit him in the back, prompting the suspect to come to a stop. As Francisco was taken into custody, officers provided him medical treatment with first aid, which saved his life. He was then promptly taken to jail. During the chase, Francisco fired approximately eight to 15 gunshots at seven different police officers. The chase lasted nearly 11 miles, in which at times the suspect drove over 100 miles per hour. Almost two years after this incident on December 1st, 2003, Francisco pleaded guilty to robbery, carjacking, attempted murder, and possession of a firearm as a convicted felon. U.S. District Judge Stephen Mary Day sentenced him to 38 years in federal prison. After spending essentially a lifetime in prison, he will be 67 years old when he is released.
